help.pageIntro: Short guides and common questions about the RaidFlow web app. Pick a chapter in the sidebar or scroll to your topic.
help.firstStepsGuestIntro: This guide shows how to sign in to RaidFlow and create a WoW character. You can add a character from the Dashboard or from your Profile. For raids, you can sign up later via the Dashboard or through Discord channels using the bot.
help.step1Text: Open the RaidFlow landing page and click “Login with Discord”. You will be redirected to Discord.
help.step2Text: On the Discord authorization page, click “Authorize” to allow RaidFlow to use your Discord account. You will then return to the web portal.
help.step3Text: Create a character under “My Characters” — either from “My Profile” or directly on the Dashboard via “+ Add character” in the “My Characters” section.
help.step4Text: In the dialog, search for the realm your character plays on and select it from the list.
help.step5Title: Find your character via BNet Sync
help.step5Text: Enter the character name exactly as in-game and click “BNet Sync”. Pick the matching character from the Battle.net list. Your Battle.net profile must not be set to “Private”.
help.step6Text: Choose class, main spec, and optionally an off-spec. If you are not on any RaidFlow Discord server, you may save the character without assigning a guild. Then click “Save”.
help.step7Text: On the Dashboard, open upcoming raids in the calendar and choose “Sign up”, or open the raid page and start sign-up there. Alternatively, use “Quickjoin” or “Sign up” on the raid post in the raid or guest channel on Discord. See the “Raid sign-up” chapter for details.
help.tipExactSpelling: Character name and realm must match WoW exactly — including special characters and capitalization.
help.tipBnetPrivate: Your Battle.net profile must be public (not “Private”), otherwise BNet Sync cannot find your character.
help.tipNoGuild: Without membership on a RaidFlow Discord server, you can still create and save a character.
help.tipGuestEligibility: To sign up you must be a guild member with raid access, or — if the raid allows guests — be eligible to join via the guest channel.
help.botSetupIntro: To use RaidFlow on a Discord server, the bot must be invited and the server must be set up once. Guild masters can then manage the guild in the web portal.
help.botSetupInviteTitle: 1. Invite the bot to your Discord server
help.botSetupInviteText: Server owners or admins invite the RaidFlow bot from the web portal:
help.botSetupInviteBullet1: On the landing page or in the burger menu, choose “Invite Discord Bot”.
help.botSetupInviteBullet2: In Discord, select the target server and confirm the requested bot permissions (manage roles, send messages, create threads, etc.).
help.botSetupInviteBullet3: The bot will then appear in the server member list.
help.botSetupSlashText: On the Discord server, run the slash command /raidflow setup. Allowed users: server owner, Administrator, or “Manage Server”.
help.botSetupSlashBullet1: The bot registers the guild in RaidFlow and stores Discord roles for guild master, raid leader, and raider.
help.botSetupSlashBullet2: Without this step RaidFlow does not recognize the server — raids and sign-ups will not work.
help.botSetupSlashBullet3: Optional: /raidflow group <name> creates a raid group (Discord role Raidflowgroup-<name>).
help.botSetupModesText: On first setup you choose how RaidFlow roles are created:
help.botSetupModesBullet1: Create standard roles — bot creates RaidFlow Guild Master, RaidFlow Raid Leader, and RaidFlow Raider.
help.botSetupModesBullet2: Map existing roles — assign existing server roles to RaidFlow roles or create individual new ones.
help.botSetupModesBullet3: Create custom roles — enter names and the bot creates the roles on the server.
help.botSetupModesReconfigure: If the server is already set up, you can change roles or restart setup.
help.botSetupWebTitle: 4. Configure the guild in the web portal
help.botSetupWebText: Users with the RaidFlow guild master role open Guild Management from the burger menu:
help.botSetupWebBullet1: Set allowed thread channels — channels where the bot may post raid messages.
help.botSetupWebBullet2: Manage raid groups and assign members (optional, for planner filters).
help.botSetupWebBullet3: Member Sync — reconcile the member list with Discord (roles, display names).
help.botSetupWebBullet4: Guild Battle.net link (optional, for character BNet Sync).
help.botSetupVerifyText: Finally, check that everything is connected correctly:
help.botSetupVerifyBullet1: On Discord: /raidflow check — shows server status, roles, bot permissions, and your mapping.
help.botSetupVerifyBullet2: In the web portal: “Check guild membership” on the Dashboard — syncs your guilds from Discord.
help.botSetupTip1: /raidflow sync manually updates roles and members (guild masters and raid leaders only).
help.botSetupTip2: Assign the correct RaidFlow roles on Discord so players can see raids and sign up.
help.botSetupTip3: Without allowed thread channels, no Discord channel can be selected when creating a raid.
help.raidSignupIntro: You can sign up for a raid in the web portal (Dashboard or raid page) or directly on the raid post in Discord. Both paths write to the same sign-up in RaidFlow.
help.raidSignupPrereqText: You need at least one character and permission for the raid: guild member with raider role in the raid channel, or — if the raid allows guests — access via the guest channel. Sign-up is only possible while the raid status is “open” or “announced” and before the sign-up deadline.
help.raidSignupWebTitle: Sign up in the web portal
help.raidSignupWebText: On the Dashboard you see upcoming raids in calendar or list view:
help.raidSignupWebBullet1: “Sign up” on a raid in the schedule — opens the raid page in sign-up mode.
help.raidSignupWebBullet2: “My sign-ups” — edit an existing sign-up or withdraw.
help.raidSignupWebBullet3: Raid detail page — set character(s), spec, attendance type, punctuality, and note, then save.
help.raidSignupWebOptionsText: The sign-up form includes among others:
help.raidSignupWebOptionsBullet1: Character and spec (main or off-spec) — multiple characters if allowed.
help.raidSignupWebOptionsBullet2: Attendance type: Attending, Reserve, Uncertain, or Declined.
help.raidSignupWebOptionsBullet3: Punctuality: On time, Might be tight, or Late (note required for “Late”).
help.raidSignupWebOptionsBullet4: Lock spec — character is only planned in the chosen spec.
help.raidSignupWebOptionsBullet5: Block reserve — prevents being moved to reserve by raid leaders.
help.raidSignupWebOptionsBullet6: Note — optional; may be required for uncertain/reserve/late or withdrawal after roster lock.
help.raidSignupDiscordText: On the raid post in the raid channel (members) or guest channel (guests), interactive buttons are available:
help.raidSignupDiscordBullet1: Quickjoin — fast sign-up with main character, default spec, attending, on time.
help.raidSignupDiscordBullet2: Sign up — step-by-step sign-up with buttons for character, spec, punctuality, and attendance type.
help.raidSignupDiscordBullet3: Help — short guide to the buttons directly in Discord (language selectable).
help.raidSignupDiscordActionsTitle: Further actions on the raid post
help.raidSignupDiscordAction1: Edit — change an existing sign-up (spec, punctuality, type, note, locks).
help.raidSignupDiscordAction2: Withdraw — remove your sign-up (reason may be required).
help.raidSignupDiscordAction3: Not attending — mark yourself absent (raid channel members only, not for guests).
help.raidSignupDiscordAction4: Info @ Raid lead — private message to the raid leader channel (only if configured).
help.raidSignupDiscordAction5: RaidTools — for raid leaders/guild masters: update post or push raid.
help.raidSignupTip1: Changes in the web portal and on Discord stay in sync — you see the same state everywhere.
help.raidSignupTip2: In the reserve-only phase after sign-up closes, only reserve sign-ups are possible.
help.raidSignupTip3: Guests use the guest channel; members use the raid channel — Quickjoin and Sign up are available in both when the raid allows it.
